name: Gisborne

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Müller-Thurgau and Gewürztraminer fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Gris sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile. Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH.

land: The high ground runs about 8°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
